references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus asks the same question about what the people went out to see—a man dressed in fine clothes—and points out that those who wear fine clothing live in kings' houses.
The preceding verse where Jesus asks what they went out into the wilderness to see, introducing a series of rhetorical questions about John.
Proverbs mentions luxury and splendor belonging to kings, which corresponds to Jesus' point that those who live in opulence and extravagance are found in royal palaces.
Esther describes the king's wealth and splendor in the palace, illustrating the life of extravagance and glory that Jesus contrasts with John's simple life in the wilderness.
Joseph was dressed in fine linen garments and placed in the king's palace, an example showing that costly clothing and luxury belong to royal surroundings.
Peter warns against outward display such as braided hair, gold jewelry, and fine clothes, urging inner beauty—a similar contrast between external splendor and spiritual value that Jesus highlights.
James describes discrimination based on fine clothing and gold rings, illustrating the same contrast between outward wealth and true godliness.
The rich man was dressed in purple and finest linen and lived in daily extravagance—an example of the luxurious life Jesus refers to as belonging in palaces.
